QUESTION:
Which setting controls the pause between two background cycles of the component that stops a single customer from using too much capacity?

DOCUMENTATION EXCERPTS:
[d0816] config | quota.interval_s | version 4.x
# `quota.interval_s`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Interval in seconds between two background runs of the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `30` |
| Available since | 3.0 |
| Component | quota |
| Unit | s |

## Tuning advice

Measure before you tune. Increase or decrease `quota.interval_s` in small steps and observe the effect for at least one day.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[quota]
interval_s = 30
```

---

- New option `ingress.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the HTTP ingress gateway that accepts messages over REST starts throttling.

- New error code PQ-E1441 (COORDINATOR_CODEC_MISMATCH) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E4572 (QUOTA_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `broker.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues, in bytes.

- New option `metrics.log_level`: log verbosity of the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics.

- New option `acktracker.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed.

- New option `quota.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant.

[d0743] config | broker.interval_s | version 4.x
# `broker.interval_s`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Interval in seconds between two background runs of the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `300` |
| Available since | 1.1 |
| Component | broker |
| Unit | s |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `broker.interval_s` only if you observe problems with the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[broker]
interval_s = 300
```

---

[d0300] config | partitioner.interval_s | version 4.x
# `partitioner.interval_s`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Interval in seconds between two background runs of the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `300` |
| Available since | 2.3 |
| Component | partitioner |
| Unit | s |

## Notes

Changes to `partitioner.interval_s` take effect after restarting the node. In clusters, use the same value on all nodes.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
interval_s = 300
```

---

[d0642] changelog | PaderQueue 2.3 release notes | version 2.3
`dlq.compression`: compression codec that the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue uses for stored or transferred data.

- New option `ingress.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the HTTP ingress gateway that accepts messages over REST.

- New option `partitioner.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written.

response.content: `quota.interval_s` controls the pause. It is the interval in seconds between background runs of the quota manager, which limits throughput per tenant.
